physical_harm: Fatal blow on the head causing brain injury and death
motive: Revenge for unauthorized entry on fields
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the trial court's findings that the accused were the aggressors who had assembled with lethal weapons and launched an assault on the complainant party, with accused No. 5 striking a fatal blow on the victim's head with the intention to kill.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses' testimony as truthful and elaborately analyzed by the trial court, which substantiated the allegations against the accused of being aggressors.

legal_representation.accused: Dr. Manish Singhvi, Sr. Adv., D.K. Devesh, Milind Kumar, Advs.
legal_representation.state: Sushil Kumar Jain, Sr. Adv., H.D. Thanvi, Rishi Matoliya (for Sarad Kumar Singhania), Advs.

investigation_status: FIR registered on 14.8.1981, case committed to Sessions Court in February 1982

appeal_history.high_court: Converted conviction under Section 302 IPC to Section 326 IPC
appeal_history.supreme_court: Modified conviction to Section 304 Part I and Section 148 IPC, sentenced to 10 years simple imprisonment

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused were the aggressors who initiated the assault with lethal weapons, and that the accused No. 5 struck a fatal blow on the victim with the intention to kill, thereby constituting murder under Section 304-I of the IPC.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the accused had exercised their right of private defence, as they were provoked by the complainant's unauthorized entry into their fields, and that the incident spiraled into a free fight without any intention to kill.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle that the right of private defence cannot be invoked if the accused are the aggressors, and that the intention to kill must be established to invoke Section 304-I of the IPC.
precedent_relied_upon: Chandrakant Patil v. State through CBI (1998) 3 SCC 38; Sumer Singh v. Surajbhan Singh & Ors. (2014) 7 SCC 323; State of Rajasthan v. Ramanand (2017) 5 SCC 695; Gottipulla Venkatasiva Subbrayanam & Ors. v. the State of Andhra Pradesh & Anr. (1970) 1 SCC 235; Deo Narain v. The State of Uttar Pradesh (1973) 1 SCC 347; Subramani & Ors. v. State of Tamil Nadu (2002) 7 SCC 210; State of Uttar Pradesh v. Gajey Singh & Anr. (2009) 11 SCC 414
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed based on the nature and gravity of the offence, the intention to kill, and the fact that the accused were the aggressors, thereby warranting a sentence under Section 304 Part I of the IPC.
judicial_aggravating_factors: The court weighed the aggravating factors of the accused being the aggressors, using lethal weapons, and the fatal blow that caused the victim's death.
other_sentence_order: The accused was directed to pay compensation of Rs.50,000/- to the next of kin of the deceased, and the period already undergone was adjusted under Section 428, Cr.P.C.
